blurb: Discovery of the dwarf planet that drove Gauß to develop least squares.

name: Perceptron Navy press conference, 1958
blurb: Press event that hyped the Perceptron as a machine that would walk, talk and be conscious.

name: Paris conference on calculating machines, 1951
blurb: Conference where Norbert Wiener played Torres Quevedo's chess machine.

name: Turing Award for deep learning, 2018
blurb: Award to Bengio, Hinton and LeCun recognizing the connectionist revival.

name: Nobel Prize in Physics, 2024
blurb: Prize to Hopfield and Hinton for neural-network foundations, cited by Schmidhuber.

name: Nobel Prize in Medicine, 1906
blurb: Cajal and Golgi shared it, cementing the neuron doctrine underpinning AI.

name: IBM PC release, 1981
blurb: Release of the IBM PC that established the Wintel standard.

name: Antikythera shipwreck recovery, 1901
blurb: Salvage that recovered the ancient geared analog computer.

name: IBM 702 debut, 1953
blurb: Debut of IBM's first commercial business computer with magnetic-core memory.

name: Decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphs, 1822
blurb: Champollion's alignment-based decipherment, a prototype of alignment-based NLP.

name: Wadi el-Hol inscriptions discovered, 1993
blurb: Discovery pushing the origin of the alphabet back to ~1850 BCE.

name: Antikythera Mechanism
blurb: Ancient geared analog computer, the world's oldest, modeling the cosmos.

name: Ishango Bone
blurb: Notched baboon fibula, a prehistoric counting/calculus device.

name: Lebombo Bone
blurb: Oldest known object used for mathematical purposes, a 29-notch tally.

name: Salamis Tablet
blurb: Oldest surviving counting board, an early external memory for arithmetic.

name: Leibniz's calculating machine
blurb: First mechanical working automatic calculating machine (stepped drum).

name: Rosetta Stone
blurb: Trilingual decree, the first multilingual parallel corpus for NLP.

name: Mark I Perceptron
blurb: Rosenblatt's hardware perceptron, the ancestor of the modern neural network.

name: SNARC
blurb: First physical artificial neural network, built by Minsky and Edmonds.

name: Homeostat
blurb: Ashby's self-organizing feedback machine demonstrating homeostasis.

name: Altair 8800
blurb: First commercially successful personal computer, a mail-order kit.

name: Deep Blue
blurb: IBM chess machine that defeated the world champion in 1997.

name: Venus of Dolni Vestonice
blurb: Among the oldest fired-clay figurines, found beside the notched wolf bone.

name: Zuse Z3
blurb: World's first functional programmable digital computer (relay-based).

name: Kempelen's Speaking Machine
blurb: Mechanical text-to-speech device, a forerunner of speech synthesis.
